name: Chola Empire
summary: A Tamil dynasty of south India that became a sea power. Its navy raided Srivijaya in 1025 and its rulers built the great temple of Thanjavur.

location.value: South India; at its height, all of the south, Sri Lanka and the Maldives, with raids to Southeast Asia.
location.source: Wikipedia: Chola dynasty (checked 6 Nov 2026); Sastri, The Cholas (1955); Britannica: Chola dynasty (checked 14 Nov 2026) (Kaveri valley core; Sri Lanka, Lakshadweep, Maldives and Southeast Asian conquests)

terrain.value: The Kaveri river delta and the Coromandel coast.

climate.value: Tropical monsoon, with rains from the north-east monsoon.

resources.value: Rice, cotton textiles, spices and pearls.

urbanisation.value: Thanjavur and Gangaikonda Cholapuram were royal capitals.

migration.value: Tamil merchant guilds (such as the Ainnurruvar) traded across Southeast Asia.

economicBase.value: Irrigated rice farming and overseas trade.

tradeRoutes.value: Indian Ocean trade to Southeast Asia and Song China.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: Gold and silver coins; land taxes recorded in detailed surveys.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Chola dynasty (checked 6 Nov 2026); Sastri, The Cholas (1955)

inequality.value: Temples and landholders controlled much wealth.

governmentType.value: An imperial monarchy with strong village self-government.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Chola dynasty (checked 6 Nov 2026); Sastri, The Cholas (1955); Britannica: Chola dynasty (checked 14 Nov 2026) (organised revenue, village self-government and irrigation)

keyRulers.value: Vijayalaya (c. 850–870), Rajaraja I (985–1014), Rajendra I (1014–1044 in Britannica; one source gives 1012) and Kulottunga I (1070–1122). Aditya Chola (r. 871–907) is credited with effectively founding the empire.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Chola dynasty (checked 6 Nov 2026); World History Encyclopedia: Chola Art and Architecture and Thanjavur (excerpt read 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: Chola dynasty (checked 14 Nov 2026) (Rajendra I start year differs by source)

succession.value: Hereditary, sometimes passing through marriage alliances (the Later Cholas).

institutions.value: Village assemblies (sabha and ur) chosen by lot, recorded at Uthiramerur.

stability.value: Stable at its height, with strong village self-government.

armyAndTech.value: A large army and navy that crossed the Bay of Bengal.

majorWars.value: Wars with the Chalukyas and the Rashtrakutas (the World History Encyclopedia says the Cholas lost several land battles to both). Naval conquest of Sri Lanka, Lakshadweep and the Maldives. Naval attack on Srivijaya: Britannica says the Cholas seized Palembang and captured the king in 1025.
majorWars.source: Sastri, The Cholas (1955); World History Encyclopedia: Naval Warfare in Ancient India (excerpt read 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: Srivijaya empire (excerpt read 13 Nov 2026); Britannica: Chola dynasty (checked 14 Nov 2026) (Britannica does not mention the 1025 Srivijaya raid; it notes Rajendra I’s conquests in the Malay region; Chalukya wars in 1046 and 1054)

territoryChange.value: Conquered Sri Lanka (c. 1017) and raided as far as the Ganges and Srivijaya.

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: the Chalukyas, Pandyas and Srivijaya.

inventions.value: Bronze statues cast by the lost-wax method, such as Shiva Nataraja.

scienceEducation.value: Temple schools and colleges taught Sanskrit and Tamil.

openness.value: Sent embassies and trade missions to Song China.

communicationTransport.value: A navy that crossed the Bay of Bengal; ports such as Nagapattinam; temple towns linked by roads.

religion.value: Hinduism, mainly Shaiva: the great royal Chola temples were dedicated to Shiva, and Nataraja was the Cholas’ clan deity. Patronage of Vaishnava and Jain communities is not checked.
religion.source: Sastri, The Cholas (1955); World History Encyclopedia: Thanjavur and Chola Art and Architecture (excerpt read 13 Nov 2026)

languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Chola dynasty (checked 6 Nov 2026); Sastri, The Cholas (1955)

artsArchitecture.value: The Brihadisvara Temple and Chola bronzes.

sharedIdentity.value: Tamil language and Shaiva Hindu culture.

dailyLife.value: Houses of brick and thatch; rice, lentils and coconut; temples were centres of daily life.

neighbours.value: The Chalukyas, Pandyas, Sri Lanka and Srivijaya.

ideasReligions.value: Spread Hindu culture and Tamil trade networks overseas.

colonisation.value: No colonies, but naval raids on Srivijaya (1025) and conquest of northern Sri Lanka.

riseSignals.value: Vijayalaya (c. 850–870) began taking over Pallava territory; Wikipedia says he took Thanjavur about 850.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Chola dynasty (checked 6 Nov 2026); Sastri, The Cholas (1955); Britannica: Chola dynasty (checked 14 Nov 2026)

peakPeriod.value: Under Rajaraja I and Rajendra I, a military, economic and cultural powerhouse of South and Southeast Asia.

declineSignals.value: Intrigue over the Pandya throne drew the Cholas in from about 1166; the Hoysalas took Chola lands from 1216, former feudatories broke away, and the Pandyas conquered the Chola country in 1257.
declineSignals.source: Sastri, The Cholas (1955); Britannica: Chola dynasty (checked 14 Nov 2026)

outcome.value: The main line ended in 1279; the Pandyas took over the Tamil country.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Chola dynasty (checked 6 Nov 2026); Britannica: Chola dynasty (checked 14 Nov 2026) (Pandyas conquered 1257; dynasty ended 1279)

overallCertainty.value: Good. Thousands of temple inscriptions survive. Second source: Wikidata starts with the early Cholas (c. 300 BCE); this app covers the imperial Cholas from c. 848.

knownFor.label: Brihadisvara Temple
knownFor.note: The great temple at Thanjavur, built under Rajaraja I.

knownFor.label: Chola bronzes
knownFor.note: Bronze statues of Hindu gods such as Shiva Nataraja, made by lost-wax casting.

knownFor.label: Chola navy
knownFor.note: A fleet that raided Srivijaya and conquered Sri Lanka.
